subject: Chemistry
source: Paraphrased exemplars in the style of Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Chemistry 1CH0 Papers 1 and 2 (2018 onwards). Stems are author-original; mark allocations follow Edexcel mark scheme conventions.

exemplars.stem: An atom of magnesium has 12 protons and 12 neutrons. State its mass number and atomic number.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: atomic number 12. 1 mark: mass number 24.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1CH0 Paper 1F style — atomic structure recall

exemplars.stem: Chlorine displaces bromine from a solution of potassium bromide. Write the balanced symbol equation for this reaction and explain why this displacement happens.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for correct formulae of reactants and products. M1 for balanced equation: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂. 1 mark: chlorine is more reactive than bromine. 1 mark: chlorine takes the place of bromine in the compound.

exemplars.stem: Explain why solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but molten sodium chloride does.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: in solid, ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice. 1 mark: ions cannot move to carry charge. 1 mark: when molten, ions are free to move and can carry charge.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1CH0 Paper 1 style — ionic compound conductivity

exemplars.stem: A student wants to obtain pure sodium chloride from a mixture of sand and salty water. Describe a method they could use.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: filter the mixture to remove the sand. 1 mark: evaporate the water (or boil/heat the filtrate). 1 mark: leave the salt to crystallise / evaporate to dryness.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1CH0 Paper 1F style — separation technique selection

exemplars.stem: Write the word equation for the reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: reactants — hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide. 1 mark: products — sodium chloride + water.

exemplars.stem: Predict the products formed at the cathode and the anode during the electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid using inert electrodes. Give the half-equation at the cathode.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: hydrogen at cathode. 1 mark: oxygen at anode. 1 mark: cathode half-equation: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. 1 mark: oxygen produced because OH⁻ ions are discharged in preference to sulfate ions.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1CH0 Paper 1H style — electrolysis half-equation (HT only)

exemplars.stem: In the Haber process, the formation of ammonia is exothermic and reversible. Predict and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the equilibrium yield of ammonia.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: predict — yield decreases. 1 mark: forward reaction is exothermic. 1 mark: increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the endothermic (reverse) direction. 1 mark: by Le Chatelier's principle, this opposes the change.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1CH0 Paper 2H style — Le Chatelier reasoning (HT only)
